gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-noto-serif: Open gaps split every word into single letters in Electroharmonix, a commanding display face. Noto Serif Hentaigana is the refined one, with open-jawed curves and small letters nearly capital-tall.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-ovo: Gaps break each word of Electroharmonix into single letters, striking and commanding, with curves that open generously. But Ovo, a text serif with a tall middle band and gentle stroke shifts, carries paragraphs with classic authority.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-domine: Aggressive and fast, Ethnocentric pushes its letters apart, with big bowls under short ascenders. Domine, a serif with compact ascenders and breathing room inside each curve, reads with dignified ease over many lines.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-esteban: Positive tracking pushes the letters of Ethnocentric apart, so its big bowls and short ascenders look fast and aggressive. Esteban, with oversized lowercase and slight stroke contrast, makes paragraphs feel settled.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-faustina: Ethnocentric pushes its big bowls and short ascenders apart with positive tracking, fast, aggressive and never clogged. Faustina, a serif, leads the eye with authority without ever dominating it.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-halant: Halant sounds authoritative and traditional, a serif with a towering x-height and terminals that point outward like tongs. Ethnocentric hits fast and hard, and Halant holds the ground beneath it.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-headland-one: Ethnocentric runs fast and aggressive, its short ascenders sitting over big bowls and its tracking pushing every letter apart. Headland One steadies the pair with dignified, well-spaced letters and gentle modulation.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-hedvig-letter: Fast, striking, spaced out: Ethnocentric pushes big bowls and short ascenders into aggressive motion. Hedvig Letters Serif brings sturdy, authoritative lowercase with plenty of room to breathe in every curve.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-lisu-bosa: Lisu Bosa reads sturdy and editorial, its tall lowercase making words look large. Against Ethnocentric, which is fast and aggressive, the text serif's spill-open counters and lightly flexed contrast make it the steadier half.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-marcellus-sc: Marcellus SC reads dignified and literary, its lowercase standing with the stature of cast iron capitals. Yet next to fast, aggressive Ethnocentric, the classic serif carries paragraphs with gentle modulation.
